title: softbank backed sb energy moves closer public markets with us ipo filing 2026 09 01
text:
Sept 1 (Reuters) - SB Energy recorded a ​66.4% revenue jump in the first half of 2026, the SoftBank-backed (9984.T)
, opens new tab
 data center developer disclosed on ‌Tuesday in paperwork for its U.S. IPO, as AI infrastructure companies flock to the public markets.
The company reported a net loss of $3.21 billion on revenue of $138.7 million in the six months ended June 30, compared with a net loss of $215.5 million on revenue of $83.3 million ​a year earlier.
Companies tied to the AI buildout have increasingly turned to the IPO market this year, ​as hyperscalers and technology firms pour billions of dollars into expanding data centers to meet ⁠soaring demand for computing.
The listing will be a key test of investor appetite for the AI infrastructure trade, which ​has come under pressure in recent weeks as concerns about the sustainability of the AI spending boom grow.
Nvidia (NVDA.O)
, opens new tab
 last week unveiled ​a rare long-term outlook of 70% revenue growth for next year, helping ease concerns that the AI boom is fading.
AI infrastructure investment by the world's largest hyperscalers is expected to exceed $1.3 trillion by 2027, according to S&P Global Ratings.
Redwood City, California-based SB Energy plans to sell new ​shares in the offering. Reuters had reported that the company could seek a valuation of more than $50 billion in its IPO, which could ​come as early as September.
Founded in 2019, SB Energy focuses on pairing power generation with data centers to help address AI's growing ‌energy ⁠constraints. The firm is partnering with OpenAI and SoftBank on a $500 billion multi-year initiative to build AI data centers for training and inference.
SB Energy had a backlog of roughly $439 billion.
Nvidia has committed to invest $1.5 billion in SB Energy in a private placement at the IPO price, according to the prospectus.
The chipmaker had earlier ​this month unveiled a $1.5 billion ​investment in SB Energy ⁠and agreed to provide a guarantee of up to $105 billion to help OpenAI lease a sprawling data center in Ohio being developed by the SoftBank-backed company.
OpenAI has also been issued warrants ​worth roughly $5.5 billion, according to SB Energy's prospectus.
The latest investments have sharpened scrutiny around ​Nvidia's financial ⁠ties across the AI industry as concerns mount over so-called circular deals between the chipmaker and its customers.
SB Energy has broadened its investor base this year, attracting new investments from Nvidia (NVDA.O)
, opens new tab
 and OpenAI. Private capital firm Ares Management (ARES.N)
, opens new tab
 has been a ⁠long-standing investor ​in the firm.
OpenAI and SoftBank earlier this year invested $500 million each in SB ​Energy as part of the Stargate initiative.
JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are among the underwriters for the offering. SB Energy will list on the ​Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas under the symbol "SBE".
